observed.facings.png: Three cut-outs of a small two-legged reptile on a checkerboard. South is the tallest and bulkiest: an upright pear-shaped body with a big round head, two large brown eyes, a closed mouth curving up at the corners, two hands held at the chest, pink shins and large three-toed feet. A single rounded knob sits on top of the skull, and a blunt lump pokes out at hip level on the viewer's right. East is a small theropod in profile, with a raised chest, a thick tail, a rounded snout, one short pointed crest at the back of the skull, tiny arms and pink lower legs. North is a rear view: back of the head with a short pointed corner at each side like two small ears, broad hips and a thick tail hanging down the middle past the feet. The hide is a regular net of olive cells with tan lines over a tan underside, with pink shins and hands.
observed.south.png: Front view, face toward the camera, standing erect like a person in a suit. Round head, two big dark brown eyes with glossy highlights, two nostrils and a wide smile-shaped mouth. One nub is centred on top of the head. Tiny hands hang at the belly. Wide pale belly, pink scaly shins and large rounded toes. The tail appears only as a blunt bulge behind the right hip.
observed.east.png: Side profile facing right. Two-legged theropod stance, body sloping up toward the head and tail held out behind. Tapered but rounded snout, a fairly large dark eye in a wrinkled reddish socket, a nearly straight mouth line, one short pointed backswept crest, tiny forelimbs at the chest and pink feet. Olive net pattern on tan.
observed.north.png: Rear view from slightly above. Back of the head without eyes or mouth, two short pale points at the upper left and right corners of the head, arms just visible at the sides, large rounded haunches, a tail tapering straight down the centre and pink feet either side. Olive net pattern covers the back and tail. The head is clearly narrower than in the south view.
observed.scale.png: The east view beside a human at max zoom, standing about half the human's height, with a body plus tail about as long as the human is wide or a little longer. In the 32 px strip it is a small tan-olive shape beside a dark rat; its tan is close to the brown ground but the head, legs and tail can still be picked out.

HEAD: partly; blunt snout and cheeks present, but the mouth turns up on south and the crest disagrees between views. EYES: two, yes, on the large side. COLOUR: no; a regular olive net on tan with no warm orange-brown patches. SIZE: roughly yes, about half the human sprite's height. REALISTIC: skin is detailed, but the south face is cute. NEGATIVE: yes, it is neither a frog nor a four-legged lizard.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it is a small pale shape with a readable head, legs and tail; the tan is close to the brown ground, but it can still be told apart.

reply.subject: RSW_Gizka
reply.image_seen: facings.png shows front, right profile and rear views of a tan-and-olive patterned biped; south.png shows a broad smiling face and upright belly; east.png shows tiny arms and a long balancing tail; north.png shows the back and tapering tail without eyes; scale.png shows the creature below the human's knee height.

concerns.evidence: South has large, rounded glossy eyes, pronounced fleshy cheeks and an upturned mouth that reads as a smile. The forelimbs are held separately against the belly, rather than clasped together, but the face clearly reads as cute.

South has one central crown projection, east has one pointed projection behind the skull, and north has two lateral projections with a shallow central dip. These do not describe a consistent single backswept crest.

South presents a tall, pear-shaped torso with the chest stacked above the belly and hind legs. East presents a longer body extending forward from the hips and a substantial balancing tail. The short tail portion visible beside the south hip could be foreshortening; the upright torso is the clearer mismatch.

The supplied 29% height spread partly reflects the more upright south pose. However, the shared-scale panel also shows a substantially broader skull in south than north, with fuller cheeks and a bulkier torso. The discrepancy extends beyond silhouette height alone.

South clearly has an upturned mouth and an erect torso, contrary to the downturned mouth and horizontal theropod body requirements. East has a rising shoulder and neck, but its trunk and balancing tail are much closer to the required build; that slope alone is less decisive.

The hide has olive scale fields separated by tan markings, with warm brown coloration on the cheeks, snout, flanks and lower tail, plus a pale belly. The pattern is regular and reticulated, but warm coloration is not confined to the hands and shins, and the hide is visibly multicoloured.

East shows a substantial head with a deep rounded cheek and a short snout ending in a blunt, rounded tip. North conceals the projecting muzzle because it shows the back of the skull. These views do not establish a missing oversized head or a pointed snout, although the cross-facing skull-width discrepancy remains covered by K4.

request.subject: RSW_Gizka

edits.change: The face is a realistic reptile face: modest, dull, side-set eyes with natural eyelids, a blunt beak-like snout, heavy fleshy cheeks, and a mouth line that turns down at the corners. The eyes are matte, without glossy highlights.

One single backswept crest sits on the midline at the rear of the skull in every view. The front view shows it as one central point above the head. The side view shows it as one rearward-sweeping point. The rear view shows it end-on as one central point.

The body is a horizontal theropod body in every view: head forward and low, torso level over strong hind legs, a thick tail tapering out behind the hips. The front view shows this same body foreshortened toward the camera, with the tail curving out visibly behind the hips.
The torso is a foreshortened horizontal theropod torso over strong digitigrade hind legs. Tiny forelimbs are tucked against the chest. A thick balancing tail is always visible.

All facings show the same animal at one scale, with the same head width, torso depth, leg length and foot size on the front, side and rear views. Only natural perspective foreshortening differs between views.

invariants: Small bipedal reptile standing on two legs
Tiny forelimbs held against the chest
Painterly vanilla RimWorld style with a clean dark outline
One consistent colour palette across all facings
request.prompt: A small bipedal reptile, the gizka, drawn as a single sprite in painterly vanilla RimWorld style: realistic, with a clean dark outline, on a transparent background. The body is a horizontal theropod body: the head is carried forward and low, the torso is level and sits over strong digitigrade hind legs, and a thick, tapering balancing tail extends out behind the hips. The head is blunt with a beak-like snout, heavy fleshy cheeks, modest dull side-set eyes with natural eyelids and no glossy highlights, and a mouth line that turns down at the corners. A single backswept crest sits on the midline at the rear of the skull. The forelimbs are tiny and tucked against the chest. The skin is matte, scaled and earthy. Front view (eyes toward the viewer): the same horizontal body foreshortened toward the camera, head forward and low, the crest as one central point, the tail curving out visibly behind the hips. Side view: the full theropod profile with the head forward, the crest sweeping back, and the tail extending behind. Rear view, seen from behind: the haunches, the thick tail base and the crest end-on as one central point, with the eyes hidden. All views show the animal at one scale, with the same head width, torso depth, leg length and foot size, differing only by natural perspective. Reference: none; build the body from this description.
